name: Blk Swan
tagline: Harbor East dining room with New American plates, cocktails, and brunch.
description: Blk Swan serves a New American menu with signature cocktails, late-morning brunch, and DJ nights in Harbor East. It is co-owned by Chris Simon and Jada McCray, with Saon Brice as executive chef.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Baltimore's Black-owned restaurant list, the 2026 Black-Owned Restaurant Tour (Feb 21 to Mar 1, 2026), and The Banner (Feb 18, 2026). Live site with OpenTable booking. Founded year 2021 from Visit Baltimore. Note: blkswan.com redirects elsewhere, so eatatblkswan.com is used. Phone left null.

name: The Urban Oyster
tagline: Jasmine Norton's oyster bar in Hampden.
description: The Urban Oyster is an oyster bar and seafood restaurant on 36th Street in Hampden. Owner Jasmine Norton opened it in 2017.

_verified.note: Black-owned per The Banner (Feb 18, 2026) and Travel Noire (Mar 28, 2025), which names Jasmine Norton as owner and gives the 2017 opening. Active per Baltimore Beat Best of 2025 (Dec 7, 2025) and live site with Resy booking.

name: Rooted Rotisserie
tagline: Rotisserie chicken and sides on Hollins Street.
description: Rooted Rotisserie cooks rotisserie chicken and sides in the Hollins Market area of Southwest Baltimore. It is run by Joseph and Amanda Burton.

_verified.note: Black-owned per The Banner (Feb 18, 2026), the 2026 Black-Owned Restaurant Tour, and Visit Baltimore's list. Live site with Toast online ordering.

name: The Land of Kush
tagline: Vegan soul food on Eutaw Street since 2011.
description: The Land of Kush serves vegan soul food in the Mount Vernon and Seton Hill area. It is owned by Gregory Brown and Naijha Wright-Brown.

_verified.note: Black-owned per The Banner (Feb 18, 2026) and Visit Baltimore's list. Founded 2011 per the business site. Live site with current menu.

name: The Avenue Bakery
tagline: Pennsylvania Avenue bakery and museum known for Poppay's Rolls.
description: The Avenue Bakery bakes Poppay's Rolls and other goods on historic Pennsylvania Avenue, and also runs a small museum about the avenue's history. It was founded by James "Jim" Hamlin, and the bakery offers tours.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Baltimore's Black-owned restaurant list and the Baltimore Times (Nov 14, 2025), which covers tours of the bakery and museum. Founded 2011 per the Visit Baltimore listing.

name: Mama Koko's
tagline: Charles Village restaurant opened in fall 2024.
description: Mama Koko's is a restaurant on East 23rd Street in Charles Village that opened in fall 2024. It is run by Angola Selassie and Ayo Hogans.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Travel Noire (Mar 28, 2025) and Visit Baltimore's list. Active per Baltimore Beat Best of 2025 (Dec 7, 2025) and live site. Founded year left null because the sources give an opening season, not a founding year. Phone left null.

name: The Empanada Lady
tagline: Afro-Latina empanadas from a Puerto Rican family recipe, downtown.
description: The Empanada Lady sells empanadas made from Elisa Milan's Puerto Rican family recipes. Milan started the business in 2016 and has had a downtown shop on South Street since 2023.

_verified.note: Black-owned (Afro-Latina owner Elisa Milan) per WMAR, Travel Noire (Mar 28, 2025), and the 2026 Black-Owned Restaurant Tour. Active per Baltimore Sun (Feb 1, 2026). Founded 2016 per the coverage. No website or phone confirmed, left null.

name: Connie's Chicken and Waffles
tagline: Chicken and waffles from the Parker brothers at Lexington Market.
description: Connie's Chicken and Waffles serves chicken and waffles and shrimp and waffles, with a stall at Lexington Market. It was started by brothers Khari and Shawn Parker.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Baltimore's list and Baltimore Magazine. Active per JHU Hub Q&A (Sep 29, 2025) and live ordering site. Founded 2016 per the business site. Waterfront Partnership also lists a Broadway Market location.

name: Matriarch Coffee
tagline: Inner Harbor coffee shop that shares profit with women coffee farmers.
description: Matriarch Coffee serves locally roasted coffee, specialty lattes, breakfast, and lunch at the Inner Harbor. Its founders say 10 percent of profit goes to women in coffee-farming communities.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Baltimore's list and the Waterfront Partnership's Black-owned list. Founders named on the Visit Baltimore listing. Live site. Founded year left null because sources disagree (2019 vs 2020).

name: Sophomore Coffee
tagline: Small coffee bar on Maryland Avenue near Station North.
description: Sophomore Coffee is a coffee bar on Maryland Avenue. Co-founder Kris Fulton was named a 2026 StarChefs Rising Star.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Baltimore Magazine's Black-owned food list (2020). Active per StarChefs profile (Feb 23, 2026) and Baltimore Beat Best of 2025 (Dec 7, 2025). Phone left null.

name: Blacksauce Kitchen
tagline: Damian Mosley's biscuits and Southern plates, open two days a week.
description: Blacksauce Kitchen is Damian Mosley's food business, known for biscuits and Southern cooking. It is open two days a week and takes online orders.

_verified.note: Black-owned per The Banner (Feb 18, 2026) and Baltimore Magazine. Live site with Toast ordering. Address left null: The Banner points to the 32nd Street Farmers Market (400 E 32nd St) while the site references 29th Street, so the current spot needs confirming.

name: Yeiboh Kitchen
tagline: Southern and Asian fusion on Maryland Avenue.
description: Yeiboh Kitchen serves Southern and Asian fusion dishes on Maryland Avenue near Station North. It opened in 2024 and is run by Deirdra Campbell and Ashlee Mack with partners Chef Chris Davis and Rodney Hueston.

_verified.note: Black-owned per the 2026 Black-Owned Restaurant Tour (Feb 21 to Mar 1, 2026). Active per that tour and Baltimore Beat Best of 2025 (Dec 7, 2025). Its own site footer still says 2024. Founded year left null.

name: Chef BobbyD Restaurant
tagline: Jamaican-American cooking on Falls Road, with a second spot in Towson.
description: Chef BobbyD Restaurant serves Jamaican-American food from a Falls Road location in Baltimore and a second location on York Road in Towson. It takes online orders.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Discover Baltimore County's Black-owned restaurant story (Jan 2025), a directory-style source. Active per that story and the live ordering site. Towson location: 6911 York Rd, (443) 938-9848.

name: Magdalena
tagline: The dining room inside The Ivy Hotel in Mount Vernon.
description: Magdalena is the restaurant at The Ivy Hotel, a small luxury hotel owned by Eddie and Sylvia Brown. It takes reservations through OpenTable.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Baltimore's African American culture guide (Ivy Hotel owned by Eddie and Sylvia Brown) and Baltimore Magazine. Active per a June 2026 wine list on the hotel site. Slug has -baltimore appended because the name is generic.

name: Good Food
tagline: Crab cakes, surf and turf, and chicken sandwiches at Harborplace.
description: Good Food serves crab cakes, surf and turf, and chicken sandwiches from the Light Street Pavilion at Harborplace. It is run under A Koi Story, the brand of local artist Koi.

_verified.note: Black-owned per the Waterfront Partnership's Black-owned list and the 2026 Black-Owned Restaurant Tour. Slug has -baltimore appended because the name is generic. Phone left null.

name: Berries by Quicha
tagline: Chocolate-covered strawberries and treats on Light Street.
description: Berries by Quicha makes chocolate-covered strawberries and gift treats, and hosts Dip, Sip and Paint sessions. It was founded by LaQuicha Brown.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Baltimore's list and Baltimore Magazine. Active per live online shop with a 2026 footer and bookable Dip, Sip and Paint sessions. Founded 2014 per the business site.

name: Last Slyce
tagline: Pizza and snowballs at Broadway Market in Fells Point.
description: Last Slyce sells pizza and snowballs from Broadway Market in Fells Point. It takes online orders.

name: Aunt Kelly's Cookies
tagline: Cookies from a Baltimore baker who started baking in 1999.
description: Aunt Kelly's Cookies is a cookie bakery on North Howard Street run by Kelly Simmons. It sells cookies online and from the shop.

_verified.note: Black-owned per Visit Baltimore's Black-owned restaurant list and its African American culture guide, which name Kelly Simmons. Draft because activity is thin: the business site footer says 2023 and has no dated posts, though its online store link is live. Address from Visit Baltimore. Founded year left null (the site says baking began in 1999, not the business).

name: Ekiben
tagline: Asian-fusion bowls and bao that began as a market cart in 2014.
description: Ekiben serves Asian-fusion bowls, buns, and noodles, and is known for its bao sandwiches. It started in 2014 as a cart at the Fells Point Farmers Market and now has several locations, including Hampden.

_verified.note: Listed as Black-owned on the Waterfront Partnership's Black-owned list (directory-style proof). The business site says it was started by college friends and names no founders, so the ownership share is unconfirmed; held as draft until ownership is verified. Address is the Hampden location from the site's order link; other locations in Fells Point, Locust Point, and Frederick. Slug has -baltimore appended because it has locations in more than one city.

name: Reginald F. Lewis Museum of Maryland African American History & Culture
tagline: Museum of Maryland African American history and culture near the Inner Harbor.
description: The Reginald F. Lewis Museum covers the history and culture of African Americans in Maryland through permanent and changing exhibitions. It opened in 2005 and is a Smithsonian Affiliate.

_verified.note: Black institution named for Reginald F. Lewis, listed in Visit Baltimore's African American culture guide. Active per 2026 exhibitions on its site (The Lines We Cross, Jul 31, 2026 to Oct 31, 2027) and an Oct 3, 2026 film showcase. Opened 2005 per Wikipedia. It is a museum, not a privately owned business.

name: National Great Blacks in Wax Museum
tagline: Wax figures of Black history on East North Avenue since 1983.
description: The National Great Blacks in Wax Museum presents wax figures and exhibits covering African and African American history. It was founded in 1983 by Drs. Elmer and Joanne Martin and hosts community events.

_verified.note: Black-founded per Wikipedia and the museum site (Drs. Elmer and Joanne Martin, 1983). Active per its events page (Voices of History Street Fair, Sep 19, 2026).

name: Galerie Myrtis
tagline: Charles Street gallery for African American and Diaspora artists.
description: Galerie Myrtis shows work by African American and African Diaspora artists in Station North. It was founded by and is run by Myrtis Bedolla.

_verified.note: Black-owned per the gallery site, which names founder and proprietor Myrtis Bedolla. Active per 2026 exhibitions on its exhibitions page.

name: Arena Players
tagline: Community theater founded in 1953, with shows at BCCC Liberty Heights.
description: Arena Players calls itself the oldest African American community theater in the country. Its McCulloh Street building is under renovation, and performances are held at the Baltimore City Community College Liberty Heights campus.

_verified.note: Black institution per its own site. Draft because the home building is under renovation (temporary office at 410 N Howard St, shows at BCCC Liberty Heights) and the 2026 to 2027 season is named but no shows are listed yet. Founded 1953 per the site.

name: Plantation Park Heights Urban Farm
tagline: Black-owned urban farm in Park Heights that takes SNAP and WIC.
description: Plantation Park Heights Urban Farm grows food in the Park Heights neighborhood and runs farm trainings. It was founded by Farmer Chippy and accepts SNAP and WIC.

_verified.note: Black-owned per its own site and the Black Farmers Index. Active per a GAP training on Apr 4, 2026 listed on its site.

name: Boyd Cru Wines

_verified.note: Black-owned per the Black Farmers Index and Baltimore Magazine. Draft because the site shows no dated 2024 to 2026 activity. Street address not confirmed, left null. Top-up 2026-10-15: address from the farm's contact page.

_verified.note: Black-owned per the Black Farmers Index, which lists it in Baltimore. Draft because the site has no dated activity and names no city, so location and current operations need confirming. Phone from the business site.

name: Black Yield Institute
tagline: Cherry Hill marketplace and food sovereignty group.

tagline: Minority depository bank serving Baltimore for over 40 years.

name: The Ivy Hotel
tagline: Small luxury hotel in Mount Vernon owned by Eddie and Sylvia Brown.
description: The Ivy Hotel is a 17-room luxury hotel in Mount Vernon with a small spa and the Magdalena restaurant. Visit Baltimore calls it the only Black-owned luxury hotel in the city.
